transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-23
Start: 16:30 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sofia (CTO Verdansk), Hank (Head Cloud Ops), Rina (Security), Caleb (SRE)

Summary: quick discovery for Private/VPC onramp. customer is evaluating Redwood Private vs Dedicated for inference workloads; primary concerns: private endpoints, cross-region access, egress IPs for compliance, and KMS integration.

Topics: private endpoints, transit gateway vs peering, region gating (APAC), SOC 2 / KMS / HSM, KV cache and latency targets, canary/pilot plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, with Ethan our solutions engineer. 
[00:12] Maya: quick roll call? 
[00:15] Sofia: hey Sofia here, CTO. 
[00:17] Hank: Hank, Cloud Ops. 
[00:19] Rina: Rina, security. 
[00:21] Caleb: Caleb, SRE. 
[00:26] Maya: perfect. objective for today is to understand your network posture and constraints for a Private onramp for our inference service, so we can propose either Redwood Private inside your VPC or a Dedicated ring with private endpoints, ok? 
[00:39] Ethan: i'll also sketch the pilot we'll run - latency buckets, token throughput, and region-specific routing. 
[00:47] Sofia: high level: we run model hosting for customer-facing features and background batch scoring. latency SLO for interactive is <=120 ms P95, cost is important but security/compliance trumps price for this project. we need isolation and full auditability. 
[01:08] Maya: got it. are you planning multi-region? i see APAC users, europe, north america? 
[01:15] Sofia: yes, primary in NA and EU, APAC is smaller but growing. for APAC we have strict region gating — some datasets can't leave APAC. 
[01:27] Ethan: two immediate flags: 1) region gating may mean we need regional Redwood Private deployments (or a Private deployment in APAC region). 2) egress IPs for outbound requests, do you have NAT/static egress? 
[01:40] Hank: we use managed NAT gateways and have a small pool of fixed egress IPs per region. we'd need those whitelisted. also we use TGW (transit gateway) to connect multiple accounts into a hub. 
[01:53] Ethan: TGW is fine — Redwood Private can peer to a TGW or we can use VPC peering depending on routing needs. TGW tends to make multi-account routing simpler but requires route table updates. 
[02:08] Rina: security questions: KMS/HSM support for keys, data at rest encryption, and audit logs. do you retain any customer data on the control plane? 
[02:21] Maya: short answer - customers control keys. we support KMS integration and can use customer-managed keys for model artifacts and logs. control plane metadata is separated and can be configured for minimal retention; we'll share the SOC2/ISO doc. 
[02:36] Rina: ok please share the exact scope in writing. also we do require proof of HSM-backed key usage in APAC for some data classes. 
[02:48] Ethan: that's a legitimate ask, we have references for HSM and KMS setups in Private — i'll attach our HSM integration note. note: in some on-prem installs we can plug into customer HSM via KMIP. 
[03:02] Caleb: on the networking side - if we do Private in our VPC, what's the recommended setup for high throughput inference? do you recommend a dedicated subnet with ENIs or do you run an endpoint-based model? 
[03:17] Ethan: for throughput and predictable latency we typically recommend a dedicated subnet with a set of GPU-backed instances behind Private endpoints; traffic enters via interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) or via direct peering into a Redwood-managed subnet depending on deployment. we keep KV cache close to the model hosts to reduce cold-start token latency. 
[03:37] Hank: one constraint — our security team won't allow cross-account peering that breaks their least-privilege policy; TGW is preferred since it centralizes controls. 
[03:48] Maya: good note. we can do a TGW attachment model or private link. TGW will require you to propagate routes to the Redwood attachment, and we'll coordinate route acceptance on Redwood side. 
[04:02] Sofia: what's the failover story? if APAC Private is overloaded or we have a region outage, do you fail over to EU/NA? that may violate data residency. 
[04:14] Ethan: we have policy-based routing. default we will not fail over across region boundaries for gated data classes. for non-sensitive traffic we can fail over to a lower-tier model in another region to preserve availability; we surface these as routing policies in the Console. 
[04:34] Rina: we also need full request/response audit logs retained 1 year and ability to export to our SIEM. 
[04:43] Maya: yes that's supported — logs can be forwarded to customer S3 (VPC endpoint) or sent to customer SIEM via secure ingest. we'll include retention config in the docs. 
[04:56] Hank: egress bandwidth: some of our inference use is high-throughput batch scoring - does Redwood support burst autoscaling on Private? 
[05:06] Ethan: yes, autoscaling and burst capacity are configurable; Dedicated customers have configurable reserved pools; for Private we can design autoscaling policies that hit your TGW attach / subnet quotas. we surface token/cost breakdowns so you can see unit economics. 
[05:22] Sofia: curious about performance — can we run a pilot with 1M tokens/day synthetic traffic and measure P95? 
[05:31] Ethan: absolutely, pilot plan i propose: 1) network pre-check (collect CIDRs, NAT IPs, TGW ARNs), 2) spin up Private cluster in a staging account in region(s), 3) run synthetic load with KV caching on/off and measure P50/P95 latency and cost, 4) review results then decide on rollout. 
[05:52] Maya: i'll send the onboarding checklist + pilot template. 
[05:57] Caleb: regarding private endpoints - do you use AWS PrivateLink endpoints or ENI peering? we prefer PrivateLink for security. 
[06:07] Ethan: PrivateLink is supported and often recommended — it gives you interface endpoints in your subnet so traffic stays within AWS private network. for TGW setups we sometimes use VPC attachments plus routing. depends on how many accounts and whether API-level isolation is required. 
[06:25] Rina: what about network egress for third-party API calls from model runtime — we have outbound firewall rules. 
[06:32] Ethan: we recommend egress via customer-managed NAT so you can control firewall / proxy egress. for calls that must go to external services we can route through your proxy with authentication. 
[06:44] Sofia: any known limits for Transit Gateway attachments or per-account ENI counts we should watch for? 
[06:50] Ethan: yes instancing numbers matter. we'll share an ops sizing doc. quick rule: plan for ENIs per GPU node and ensure subnet IP availability for peak scale; TGW attachment ENI quotas and route table propagation scales with number of attachments. 
[07:06] Hank: curious about image/OSI controls — how does deployment model keep model artifacts private? are images pulled from our ECR or from Redwood image repo? 
[07:15] Ethan: we can support both. for Private you can bring your own container images from your ECR via role-based access; alternatively Redwood can use signed images with customer-managed keys. artifacts at rest are encrypted. 
[07:29] Rina: and for audit — can individual token-level traces be redacted before going to logs? we need PII suppression. 
[07:36] Maya: yes we have hooks for data redaction and custom transformers. we also support evals against a test prompt set to detect regressions. we'll include a note on redaction pipelines. 
[07:50] Sofia: pricing — do you have a different pricing model for Private vs Dedicated? 
[07:55] Maya: Private is licensed (platform fee) + usage for reserved capacity + optionally support. Dedicated is more usage/reservation based. we'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up. 
[08:06] Ethan: one more for the SREs — KV cache warmup: when you route similar prefixes we cache KV to reduce repeated compute for multi-turn chats. that impacts network in that cache nodes should be co-located with inference nodes for lowest latency. 
[08:22] Caleb: noted. for pilot we'll run with and without cache. 
[08:26] Maya: ok next steps recap: ethan will run a network deep dive w/ your SREs for TGW/PrivateLink details; i'll send SOC2, KMS/HSM notes, and the onboarding checklist; you will share VPC CIDRs and egress IPs. any other asks? 
[08:45] Sofia: please include an example route table and a minimal set of security group rules we should open. 
[08:52] Ethan: will do. i'll also bring a short runbook for failover behavior per routing policy. 
[08:58] Rina: we'll want a security contact for any compliance follow-ups. 
[09:02] Maya: that's me — i'll be the PD contact and put Ethan and our security PM on the thread. 
[09:08] Hank: timeline: if pilot hits metrics we want to move to prod in Q1. 
[09:14] Maya: great. we'll aim to turn around the docs and schedule the deep dive this week. 

[09:25] End of call notes: transcription has a few mis-heard words (company names), will attach raw recording. references shared during call: https://redwood.ai/docs/private-onramp, https://redwood.ai/security/soc2, pilot-template.xlsx (link hosted), network-sizing.pdf (link).

Quick pilot checklist (inline):
- collect VPC CIDRs, NAT egress IPs, TGW ARNs
- decide on PrivateLink vs TGW attachment
- confirm KMS/HSM requirements and key owner
- set up staging Private cluster in requested region(s)
- run synthetic traffic 1M tokens/day with cache toggles
- export logs to customer's S3 and SIEM for audit

Action items (restated):
- Maya: send onboarding + security docs (SOC2 + HSM note) by 2027-11-26
- Ethan: schedule TGW/peering deep dive with Verdansk SREs by 2027-11-30
- Hank: provide VPC CIDR and egress IP list by 2027-11-29

Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
